subject: Anyone calculate spectral density of a time series using spec.pgram?

messages.author: a9ef27568b219b48
messages.subject: Anyone calculate spectral density of a time series using spec.pgram?
parts:
Hi all,

This might be a long shot, but I'm wondering if anyone here has worked with the spec.pgram() package to calculate spectra of a time series. I'm using spec.pgram to generate spectral density plots (aka: frequency content plots or smoothed periodogram plots), but I'm running into a simple (but important) problem - I'm not sure if the output from the spec.pgram() package is already log transformed or if I have to do that.

This documentation says the package defaults to log scale (see pg 6, Spectral Analysis in R). https://ms.mcmaster.ca/~bolker/eeid/2010/Ecology/Spectral.pdf

But looking through these online examples, it looks like the author plots the output on a log scale: https://rstudio-pubs-static.s3.amazonaws.com/9428_1197bd003ebd43c49b429f22ea4f36e5.html  

If you use a different package to calculate spectral density of a time series I'd still be interested to hear what you use and if the output is automatically log transformed.  

Many thanks in advance for your help, tips, and advice!

Best,
Mikaela

--
Mikaela Provost
Graduate Group in Ecology
University of California, Davis
